copies.headline: Adam Loses One, Still Owns Everything
copies.body: Adam is 6-1, averaging 144.0 a game, first of 12 in scoring, and his all-play record is 62-15 — an 80% win rate against the entire league every week. That is not luck; his +0.4 is about fair. Week 7's 103.0 was his season low and snapped the run, which in this context qualifies as a human moment. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Jayden Daniels and Kenneth Walker III anchor a roster projecting 136 a week, first of 12. The 89 draft grade was the warning shot. Isaac gets him next.

copies.headline: John Scores Like a Contender, Drafted Like Nobody
copies.body: The numbers don't lie about John: 128.4 a game, second of 12, and a 50-27 all-play that says the 4-3 record is actually selling him short — luck has him half a win underwater. Over the last three weeks he's gone 24-9 all-play despite a 100.1 stinker in there. The weird part is he built this out of a draft that graded 80, T-9th of 12, and a roster projecting 115 a week, 10th of 12. Puka Nacua and Kyren Williams carrying a lot. Week 8 is Peter, who John leads 6-3 all-time.

copies.headline: Leif's Three-Game Streak Keeps Outrunning The Math
copies.body: Leif is 5-2 on a W3 run with the 4th-best scoring average at 123.4, which is genuinely good, and also his all-play is 42-35 and his luck sits at +1.2 wins, 3rd-highest in the league. Both things are true. The last three weeks tell the story: 164.3, then 112.3, then 92.9, trending the wrong direction while the record improves. The draft-night roster graded 80, 12th of 12, and the lineup projects 117 a week, T-7th. Josh Allen and Derrick Henry are carrying real weight here. McCaffrey and Montgomery are questionable, and Week 8 projects 95 against Kaleb. Keep winning anyway.

copies.headline: Third in Scoring, 2-5, Zero Justice
copies.body: Christian is scoring 126.9 a game, 3rd of 12, with an all-play record of 46-31 — also 3rd. His actual record is 2-5. Luck sits at -2.2 wins, 12th of 12, which is the statistical way of saying the schedule has been mugging him weekly. The 89 draft grade, T-2nd of 12, is holding up: CeeDee Lamb, Chase Brown and Trevor Lawrence project this roster at 126 a week, 2nd of 12. The only real complaint is the last three weeks — 103.1, 124.3, 122.3, a 52% all-play. Fine, not fatal. CJ's next.

copies.headline: Logan Is Scoring Fine, Losing Anyway
copies.body: Logan is 2-5 with a 44-33 all-play record — 4th of 12 — and 963.1 points against, the most anyone has absorbed. That is a luck figure of -2.0 wins, 11th-luckiest of 12, which is the statistical version of getting mugged in a parking lot. The last three weeks he's gone 142.3, 152.5, 118.9 and posted a 25-8 all-play, best in the league over that stretch. The concern is forward-looking: Joe Burrow, Justin Jefferson and Jaylen Warren project to 116 a week, 9th of 12. Isaiah Likely at zero isn't helping.

copies.headline: Grant's 158.6 Finally Matches The Volume
copies.body: Grant has spent seven weeks being an average scorer with a great schedule — 115.1 a game, sixth in the league, but only 732.9 points against, second-fewest. That gap is the whole 4-3. The all-play says 37-40, which is the honest version. Then Week 7 happened: 158.6, a season high, and suddenly the last three weeks are a 21-12 all-play. The roster projects 119 a week, fifth of twelve, with Amon-Ra St. Brown questionable. Logan's next. Draft grade was a T-9th 80, so this is earned, not inherited.

copies.headline: 5-2 Built On Opponents, Not Offense
copies.body: Peter is 5-2 and almost none of it is his doing. The 780.9 points for ranks 8th of 12; the 714.8 against is the fewest in the league, and the +2.0 luck is the league's best. All-play says 33-44, 43%, 9th of 12 — and the last three weeks (95.4, 69.8, 114.6) produced a 6-27 all-play, 18%, worst in the league. The draft was genuinely elite, 89 out of 100, 1st of 12, and the roster still projects 124 a week, 3rd of 12. Lamar Jackson is questionable. Week 8 is John. The 6-3 lead looms.

copies.headline: 5-2 On Paper, 34-43 In Reality
copies.body: Kaleb is 5-2 and the schedule deserves most of the credit: 109.2 points a game, 9th of 12, against the 3rd-fewest points allowed in the league, and +1.9 wins over expected, 2nd-luckiest of 12. The all-play record is 34-43, which is the honest version. The 131.5 last week was real and snapped a stretch of 85.7 and 94.4, but the roster projects 114 a week, 11th of 12, and that's with Breece Hall questionable. The 86 draft grade tied for 4th and hasn't translated. Leif's next, 112 projected. Enjoy the record while it lasts.

copies.headline: CJ's 4-3 Is Held Together With Tape
copies.body: The record says contender, everything else says otherwise. CJ is 4-3 with an all-play mark of 38-39, which is the 6th-best scoring profile in a 12-team league — fine, average, unremarkable — and a +0.5 luck figure that explains the gap. Week 7's 90.9 was the season low and the slide started earlier: 42% all-play over three weeks. Worse, this roster projects to 111 a week, 12th of 12, and Jonathan Taylor can't carry a tight end room projecting zero. Week 8 projects 98 against Christian. The tape is uglier than the standings.

copies.headline: Season High Arrives, All-Play Still Hates Them
copies.body: Isaac won, which is nice, and the 126.5 in Week 7 was his season high, which is nicer. Everything underneath it is ugly. 103.6 a game is 11th of 12, the all-play is 25-52 — 32 percent, also 11th — and 3-4 exists partly because he's sitting +0.7 wins above expectation, fourth-luckiest in the league. The roster isn't the problem: Ja'Marr Chase, Javonte Williams, a healthy-ish Saquon Barkley, 117 a week projected. Isaac just keeps leaving 79-point weeks on the board. Week 8 draws Adam with a 112 projection. Good luck.

copies.headline: Postseason Assassin Needs A Postseason First
copies.body: Noah's 102.5 per game is 12th of 12, and the all-play says it isn't bad luck — 24-53, 31%, also 12th. The -1.2 luck figure means he's been losing games he deserved to lose. The strange part: this roster projects for 118 a week, 6th of 12, and the draft graded out at 86, T-4th. Drake Maye, James Cook III, Garrett Wilson — that's a lineup, not a salvage yard. Last three weeks he's all-played 52%, which is progress. At 1-6, progress is a hobby, not a plan.

copies.headline: Good Roster, Bad Everything Else, Mitchell
copies.body: The roster projects for 120 a week, 4th of 12, and Mitchell is 1-6 with an all-play mark of 27-50. That gap is the whole story. The last three weeks — 132.9, then 85.5, then 79.4 — went 8-25 all-play, 24%, and that's not variance, that's a lineup falling apart in real time. Jahmyr Gibbs projects 25 and the supporting cast keeps showing up questionable. His luck sits at -1.5 wins, which is the one honest defense available. Week 8 is Noah. Start measuring the dress.

intro: Adam is at the top and it isn't close — 77.7 to John's 59.1, with 144.0 a game and an 80% all-play mark that says he'd be winning this league under any scoring system you invented. Mitchell holds the bottom at 35.4, and the cruel part is it's not even bad luck doing it: 106.7 a game, 35% all-play, and a 24% form number that means the 1-6 is mostly earned. Leif made the week's cleanest jump, 5th to 3rd on the back of a 5-2 record, though the +1.2 luck and 54% all-play suggest he's renting that spot rather than buying it. The other direction belongs to CJ, who fell 6th to 9th and now sits 46.1 to Kaleb's 46.5 — four tenths from climbing back out, which is either encouraging or infuriating depending on his mood.
